title: The component plan says which keys, flags and coordinate rule each slice uses
goal: A plan for building components already exists and says what a component is, how copies stay linked, and in what order the pieces get built. Three things it does not say would each be guessed differently by whoever builds next: where a piece inside a group thinks it is, which menu items and keyboard shortcuts each step adds, and which switch in the Experiments window turns each step on. Fill those in so the ladder is built one way.
notes:
RETARGETED by the 2026-09-03 retriage. The original task asked for a new page, docs/design/next-components.md. While it sat in the queue, docs/design/ui-building.md was written and it already covers the IA (one tree, Library as a panel group, main/instance/override/variant, styles), the nine step order of work, the deferred list and the user decisions. Writing a second page now would be two sources of truth for the same ladder, so this task shrank to the three gaps that page has: no coordinate rule, no menu items or shortcuts, no flag names.

The coordinate rule is the one that has to be settled first, because layers-can-hold-layers is built straight after this and encodes it. The recommendation already written into that task is that a child frame is relative to its parent, which is what an instance needs: a main is placed at many spots and its children cannot each carry canvas coordinates.

Photoshop parity on the keys (user preference): Command G groups, Shift Command G ungroups. Option Command K for Make Component is what the component task assumes.

Objective: ui-components (staged now, under the focus). It is the spec the rest of the ladder is built from, and it earns its place by stopping four later slices from each inventing a different answer.
acceptance: docs/design/ui-building.md states whether a layer inside a group stores its position against its parent or against the whole picture, and why, in one short section
It lists, per step in The order of work, the menu items and keyboard shortcuts that step adds, using the Photoshop shortcut where one exists
It names the feature flag each step ships behind, and whether that flag is on by default in Next
It says what the first version deliberately does not do, so later work is not judged against a promise nobody made
No second component page is written: everything lands in the existing document
